conviction_note: The evidence is balanced. On the negative side, mortgage rates rose to 7.40% (from 6.34% a year ago) on a builder whose main incentive is rate buydowns, peer orders were weak (LEN -9%, KBH -12%), and Q3 deliveries look slightly tight against backlog. On the positive side, there is an easy orders comp (Q3 2025 was -6%), MHO's Midwest-heavy footprint fits Census Midwest new-home sales +22.5% YoY and LEN Central orders +4%, short interest has built (DTC 7.4), and the balance sheet supports a buyback. So p_up is 48 on abs 4.5, which gives -0.18. The findings sum to +0.10 because the rates negative is shrunk for agreeing with the skew and the -13% run-up, while p_up still leans slightly bearish on the margin line the stock trades on. The gap is small and both numbers are close to zero on purpose.
bar: Q3 2026 EPS $3.25 and revenue $1.11B (MarketBeat preview 2026-10-14, https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-mi-homes-mho-set-to-post-earnings-on-wednesday-2026-10-14/; TipRanks also $3.25; Benzinga $3.31 / $1.11B, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/MHO/earnings-forecasts; AAII/I-B-E-S $3.30 from 4 analysts, https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/522545-what-you-need-to-know-about-mi-homes-incs-q3-earnings; Earnings Whispers is the outlier at $3.05-3.15). Two sources agree, so the bar counts as sourced. The company gives no quantified quarterly guidance (Q2 release: 'well positioned to have a solid 2026'; ~5% average community count growth for 2026). Year-ago Q3 2025: EPS $3.92, revenue $1.1B, 2,296 deliveries, 1,908 new contracts (-6%), gross margin 23.9%. print_vs_bar_pct is measured on revenue.
positioning_check: Short interest is 1,495,501 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, 7.36 days to cover, ~5.9% of shares outstanding. It is up from 1,241,048 on 2026-07-31, so shorts built about 20% after the last print (https://equibles.com/stocks/mho/shortinterest; the next FINRA release is due 2026-10-26). Borrow fee was ~0.3% in mid-2026 (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/mho/). This is moderate and building, not crowded. Baseline skew is +7.16 vol points (downside paid), but the chain is unusable: ATM spread 81% of mid, total OI 126, put/call OI 0.1. Treat the skew as a weak statement. Tape: -13.0% over 20 days, -19.7% since the 2026-07-29 print (AAII), 5.4% above the 52-week low, 23.9% below the high.

findings.finding: The 30-year mortgage rate (Freddie Mac PMMS) climbed through and after the quarter: ~6.8% at end-August (Lennar), 7.03% on Sep 24, 7.28% on Oct 1, 7.40% on Oct 8 and Oct 15, against 6.34% a year earlier. M/I says rate buydowns are its primary incentive and it will 'continue to promote with such buy-downs for the foreseeable future'. Late-Q3 incentive cost and Q4/2027 margin commentary therefore lean negative against a bar ($3.25) that needs EPS up from Q2's adjusted $3.14 at a roughly flat ~22% gross margin.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 (2025-10-22): margin down 320bp to 23.9% with orders -6%, and the stock fell -6.14%, the largest move in the 7-print history. The three prints since (Jan, Apr, Jul 2026) with stabilising margins rose +2.9%, +3.7% and +1.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The rate rise is public and homebuilders have sold off (MHO -13% in 20 days, -20% since the last print; LEN -14% in a month per MarketBeat 2026-09-16). What is not public is how much buydown cost per closing MHO absorbed in September and what it says about Q4 margin. If that were fully priced, the bar would have come down. Instead consensus Q3 EPS ($3.25-3.31) still sits above Q2's $3.14, and the AAII revisions score is negative (-2.5% FY over 3 months) but the quarter bar has not been cut.
findings.independence: The company's buydown reliance is from its Q2 call (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/mi-homes-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-07-30/ snippet; HousingWire 2026-08-04 https://housingwire.com/articles/mi-homes-earnings-q2-2026 says buydowns are 'costly but hard to avoid'). Lennar 8-K 2026-09-16: 'environment ... has deteriorated', rates increased through the quarter (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000920760/000162828026062287/ex991-2026831x8kq3.htm). This is macro-to-company transmission and is not confirmed by MHO.

findings.finding: Peers that reported after MHO's July 29 print show weaker national demand over June-August: Lennar new orders -9% YoY to 20,879 (missed its own 21,000-22,000 guide), full-year deliveries cut to 80-81k, East -17%, South Central (Texas) -14%. KB Home net orders -12% with absorption down to 3.1/community/month from 3.8. MHO's Florida, Texas and Carolinas division (its Southern region) sits in LEN's two weakest regions.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Orders are the line that drove the Q3 2025 -6.14% (orders -6%). Q2 2026's record +15% orders bought +1.54%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. Both peer prints are a month old and the sector sold off on them. The residual is that MHO's Southern half may show the same softness that the Q2 record (+15%) did not, and consensus has not been cut for the quarter.
findings.independence: KB Home Q3 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000795266/000079526626000068/exh991kbh-earningsrelease0.htm, Sept 2026) is a different document pointing the same way. The Lennar document is also used in findings 1 and 3, for different lines (rates and Central region).

findings.finding: MHO's Midwest-heavy footprint (Ohio, Indiana, Illinois, Minnesota, Michigan) is where demand held up. Census August new single-family sales in the Midwest were 98k SAAR, +22.5% YoY (South +3.4%), and Lennar's Central region orders rose 4% YoY while every other Lennar region fell 9-17%. Add an easy comp (Q3 2025 MHO orders 1,908, -6%) and MHO's record Q2 pace of 3.4/community with cancellations at 8%, and Q3 orders are likely up YoY.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A record Q2 orders print (+15%) bought +1.54% on 2026-07-29. Q1 2026 (+2.9% on 2026-01-28) and Q2 (+3.7% on 2026-04-22) also rose. The orders decline in Q3 2025 cost -6.14%.
findings.why_not_priced: The sector trades as one basket on rates and on LEN/KBH's national -9%/-12%. MHO is down as much as LEN in the last month despite a regional mix that LEN's own table shows was the only growing region. If the market had priced the regional split, MHO would have held up better than LEN and KBH, and it has not (-13% in 20 days).
findings.independence: Lennar 8-K regional orders table, Central +4% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000920760/000162828026062287/ex991-2026831x8kq3.htm). The Census Midwest series is noisy (±large CI, July revised 43k to 53k). MHO's own Q2 monthly orders were +13%/+23%/+9% (April/May/June; HousingWire https://housingwire.com/articles/mi-homes-earnings-q2-2026), showing June deceleration. Both of these are proxies; this is not MHO's own Q3 number.

findings.finding: Backlog arithmetic from the Q2 release: June 30 backlog was 2,426 homes (-6% YoY) at a $538K average, and the Q2 average closing price was $459K (vs $479K). Hitting $1.11B of revenue (flat vs Q3 2025's $1.1B on 2,296 deliveries) needs ~2,330-2,380 deliveries, i.e. ~96-98% conversion of beginning backlog plus spec sold-and-closed in the quarter. Q3 2025 converted 89%; Q2 2026 converted ~98% (implied March 31 backlog ~2,245). Revenue is achievable but leaves little room, so I lean to a slight miss (~-1%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 revenue -8.5% YoY with an EPS beat of 1c bought +1.54%. Revenue has not been the line this name traded on; orders and margin have.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus revenue of $1.11B sits flat YoY although beginning backlog is down 6% and ASP is down ~4%. A consensus that had absorbed the backlog would sit nearer $1.07-1.09B. This is my inference from the primary document, and the spec-heavy model (78% of Q2 orders were spec) can close the gap.
findings.independence: Q3 2025 comparison from the 2025 Q3 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/799292/000079929225000073/exhibit991earningspressrel.htm). This finding rests on the same Q2 release that supplies the community count in finding 7, but on a different line.

findings.finding: Short interest rose ~20% after the last print, from 1.24M (2026-07-31) to 1.50M shares (2026-09-30), now 7.4 days to cover, while the stock fell ~20% to within 5.4% of its 52-week low at 10x trailing EPS. Shorts are positioned for a bad print, so an in-line orders/margin print can squeeze.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not directly observable. The last three prints, all into weak tapes, rose modestly (+1.5% to +3.7%).
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the mechanism, not a fact the price absorbs. ~6% of shares short with 7+ days to cover on 227k average daily volume means covering adds pressure if the print is not bad. It is moderate, not crowded, hence the small size.
findings.independence: AAII 2026-10-20: stock -19.7% since 7/29 vs SPY +5.5%, P/E 10.3 vs industry 12.9 (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/522545-what-you-need-to-know-about-mi-homes-incs-q3-earnings).

findings.finding: M/I has net cash and an undrawn $900M facility, and bought back $50M of stock in Q2 alone. Homebuilding debt-to-capital is 18% and net debt-to-capital about -1%, with $735.9M of cash. With the stock ~17% below the $148-150 at which the CFO sold in early August, a larger Q3 buyback or a new authorization is likely to be disclosed in the release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Buybacks have been routine at M/I. No separable reaction is on record.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q3 repurchase amount is unknown until the release. A step-up at lower prices would be new information, and no estimate source carries buyback size.
findings.independence: Same Q2 release as findings 4 and 7, used for a different line. No independent source.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call management kept its plan for about 5% average community count growth in 2026, with openings weighted to the second half, while the Q2 count was flat YoY at 234. Q3 should show the count rising, which supports orders and the 2027 delivery outlook.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no specific record. Community growth commentary has been part of the stable prints in 2026.

findings.why_not_priced: This sits inside what the company already guided, so most of it is expected. The residual is whether openings came through on schedule in a deteriorating market.
findings.independence: Q2 release shows 234 communities at June 30 in both years (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000799292/000079929226000025/exhibit991earningspressrel.htm).

baseline_tension: The negatives (rates, weak national peer orders) agree with the positive skew (downside paid, though the chain is unusable) and the -13% run-up, so they are largely priced. The positives (Midwest mix, easy comp, short build, buyback) cut against the tape. On balance the evidence is near zero with only a slight bearish lean in p_up.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (sign agreeing with skew and run-up): the rates/buydown negative went from -0.8 to -0.6 because it agrees with the downside skew and the -13% run-up. Short interest was checked: 5.9%, 7.4 DTC, moderate, so other negatives were left alone.
Lesson 5 (proxy vs company number): the Midwest-mix positive went from +0.8 to +0.6 because it rests on Census and Lennar regional proxies, not MHO's own Q3 number.
Lesson 3 (own caveat reaches the number): the CFO Form 4 finding went from -0.1 to 0.0 because its own text calls it routine and priced.
Lesson 6: two agreeing estimate sources ($3.25 MarketBeat and TipRanks) give a sourced bar, so no cap applied. p_up moved from 47 to 48 after the rates negative was shrunk.
Left standing: the peer-orders finding, the backlog arithmetic, positioning, buyback and community count.
